answer: Like the fable of one shepherd claiming a whole meadow of flocks, a sybil operator pretends one server is many agents. The network can test this physically: each epoch, randomly chosen beacon nodes ping every identity and time the round trips. Light speed bounds how far each agent can be, so the delays triangulate a rough location. Dozens of keys answering from one rack show matching timing fingerprints and share a single reward slot, while honest agents spread like caves through karst show distinct, stable signatures.
